candidates.context: Investigational new drug applications (INDs) for antibiotic drugs submitted under 21 CFR part 31 The recommendations in this guidance are not intended to be applied retrospectively to antibiotic 34 drugs submitted in applications or their supplements, or to antibiotic drugs marketed before 35 finalization of this guidance. This is to prevent potential manufacturing discontinuances or 36 interruptions of marketed antibiotic drugs that could lead to supply chain disruptions. However, 37 applicants and manufacturers of marketed antibiotic drugs should consider updating impurity 38 specifications in accordance with this guidance when making major changes, such as replacing a 39 source of active ingredient(s), and to ensure the drugs are manufactured in compliance with 40 Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) requirements. 41

candidates.statement: Applicants and manufacturers of antibiotics produced entirely by chemical synthesis should 87 follow the principles described in the above guidances for controlling impurities and degradation 88 products. However, many antibiotics are derived through fermentation processes or semi- 89 synthetic methods rather than chemical synthesis. The complex processes involved in 90 fermentation and semi-synthetic methods can introduce a wider variety of potential impurities 91 compared to chemical synthesis. Despite the use of these methods to produce antibiotics, 92 available guidances do not provide recommendations for the control of impurities and 93 degradation products in drugs produced by fermentation or semi-synthetic processes, including 94 certain antibiotics. To address this gap, this guidance outlines recommendations for identifying, 95 qualifying, and controlling impurities and degradation products in fermentation-based and semi- 96

candidates.statement: Antibiotics produced by fermentation or semi-synthesis typically result in more complex drug 104 substances compared to those made solely by chemical synthesis. The complexity stems from the 105 use of biological systems, which generate a mixture of compounds during manufacturing. 106 Antibiotic drug substances produced by these methods can contain a mixture that includes the 107 active ingredient and impurities. The active ingredient is generally not a single molecular entity 108 but rather a collection of structurally related, biologically active analogs that together define the 109 active ingredient. These mixtures should be fully characterized to identify impurities and 110 antibiotic-related analogs 17 in the drug substances, as well as degradation products in the drug 111 products. 112
candidates.context: To comply with CGMP regulations, scientifically sound and appropriate specifications 18 must be 114 established to ensure that drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, 115 quality, and purity. 19 This process includes setting tests and acceptance criteria for degradation 116 products. Likewise, drug substance specifications should include tests and acceptance criteria for 117 impurities. 20 Implementing these controls is crucial for ensuring consistent production of high- 118 quality antibiotic drugs. 119

candidates.context: Specifications, standards, sampling plans, and testing procedures for drug products must be 153 scientifically sound and appropriate to ensure they conform to appropriate standards. 24 21 Specified degradation products in drug products can be identified or unidentified. Refer to ICH Q3B(R2) for the threshold-based approach that could be used for the reporting, identification, and/or qualification of degradation products in drug products. candidates.statement: Likewise, drug substance specifications should be scientifically sound and appropriate to ensure 160 drug substances meet established standards of quality and purity. 27 Applicants and manufacturers 161 should document: 1) a description of the analytical procedures used to test for impurities in drug 162 substances, and 2) evidence that the analytical procedures have been validated and are suitable 163 under actual conditions of use. Reference standards used in the analytical procedures for control 164 of impurities and degradation products should be evaluated and characterized according to their 165 intended uses. 28
candidates.context: 26 See 21 CFR 211.165(e) and 211.194(a)(2). The validation of analytical procedures for evaluating impurities and degradation products 168 should be carried out in accordance with the ICH guidance for industry Q2(R2) Validation of 169 Analytical Procedures (March 2024). This entails assessing various parameters such as 170 specificity, range, accuracy, precision, and robustness. Specifically, the reportable range 171 assessment involves establishing linearity and validating lower range limits, including detection 172 limit and quantitation limit. Furthermore, specificity assessment should involve demonstration of 173 stability-indicating properties using samples collected from stress testing , 29 if appropriate. 174
